author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Reuters poll shows a strong consensus that the Bank of Japan will raise its policy rate to 1.25% on September 18 as officials confront broadening inflation pressure and a weak yen.

All but two of 68 economists surveyed from September 1 through September 8 expected an increase, a 97% share that was substantially higher than in the prior poll. More than one-third of respondents also expected another increase to 1.50% in October or December.

Looking further ahead, 57 of 64 economists expected the rate to reach at least 1.50% by the end of March. About 62% projected a level of at least 1.75% by the end of the second quarter of 2027, three months earlier than the previous survey indicated.

The poll is a forecast, not a policy decision. A faster tightening path can influence the yen, Japanese government bonds and global capital flows, particularly strategies that rely on borrowing cheaply in Japan to invest elsewhere.
dek: Ninety-seven percent of economists surveyed expect a September 18 move to 1.25%, with a faster path toward 1.75% next year.
headline: Reuters poll points to Bank of Japan rate increase this month
